newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 12.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
RED ALERT IN BIHAR FOR 48 HOUR STRIKE

A red alert has been sounded in Bihar on the eve of the 48-hour state strike called by 15 leftwing parties, including the Communist Party of India and the Communist Party of India (Marxist). The strike has been called in support of their demand for the resignation of state chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested four top Bihar officials and a retired bureaucrat in the fodder case. They were produced before the special judge, who remanded them to custody.
The Hindustan Times
I-T COMMISSIONER OF CALCUTTA HELD

The income tax commissioner of Calcutta was arrested from his office in connection with the Bihar fodder case. The arrested income tax commissioner was produced before the acting chief metropolitan magistrate in Calcutta. He was remanded to police custody with the direction that the CBI should produce the accused before the special court in Patna.
The Economic Times
EUROPEAN UNION GEARING UP FOR DISPUTE SETTLEMENT

The European Union is gearing up for a dispute settlement proceeding with India for not agreeing to a shorter time frame for lifting quantitative restrictions (QRs) on imports. The EU is also upset that India has shunted more than 75 percent of its priority products into the second and third phases for lifting QRs which would mean between 2000 and 2006. The EU is looking at a two or three year time frame for the complete removal of QRs. EU sources said they were making no headway as the second day of talks at the World Trade Organisation balance of payments committee meetings began in Geneva on Wednesday.
STATE BANK OF INDIA SUSPENDS 3 OFFICERS IN CRB SCAM

The State Bank of India suspended three of its officials, charging them with procedural lapses leading to the bank losing about 580 million rupees in the CRB Capital Markets scandal. The suspension triggered off a flash strike by officers of the bank's leading branches. The officers have also called for an indefinite strike if the management does not withdraw the suspension orders immediately. The suspension notices were delivered to the officials at their home late at night by a special courier. The officials were working in the bank's Bombay main branch. All the three are junior officials.
TELECOMMUNICATIONS TARIFF POLICIES TO BE REVIEWED

The tariff policies of the Department of Telecommunications are expected to be reviewed very soon is due to the decrease in revenue per line. The average revenue per telephone line a month up to January 31 this year was 909 rupees as against an average revenue per line a month of 930 rupees during 1995/96 (April-March) and 923 rupees during 1994/95. In a recent meeting of the heads of telecom circles, they pointed out that there had been no increase in the tariff since May 1993 while the subsidy for rural telephones was substantially increased.
EXPORTS GET RESPITE IN RECOGNITION CRITERIA

The Commerce Ministry has given a year's respite to exporters on the eligibility criteria for export houses, trading houses, star trading houses and super star trading houses. The decision will affect most exporters in the country. As per a notification from the directorate general of foreign trade, the eligibility criteria based on an average FOB value of exports made during the last three licensing years has been brought down to 125 million rupees, 625 million rupees, 3,125 million rupees and 9,375 million rupees for 1997/98 (April-March) for the different trading houses.
MAHARASHTRA WILL GIVE NO MORE GUARANTEES TO IPPS

The Maharashtra state government will not provide any more financial guarantees to independent power projects (IPPs) in the state. The state guarantee for the first stage of the Enron power project is worth 15 billion rupees. Using that as a benchmark, guarantees to the 410 megawatt Patalganga project and 1,082 megawatt Ispat project will amount to another 27 billion rupees. Stating that the developers will have to be ready to take on more risks, the state energy secretary said the escrow account mechanism is not a feasible option for risk mitigation.
Financial Express
MODI RUBBER SHELVES JV PLAN WITH CONTINENTAL

Modi Rubber (MRL) and international tyre major Continental AG of Germany have shelved their proposed radial tyre project. Modi Rubber instead plans to import and market radial tyres in the domestic market. At present, MRL manufactures only cross-ply tyres. But it is keen to enter the radial segment as part of its long-term plans. Company sources said the joint venture proposal has been shelved due to financial constraints and the decision of financial institutions to stop any further lending assistance to MRL. MRL has reported a loss in the first six months ended December 1996.
